official.deadline_note: Alberta Innovates publishes no single central deadline: the programme page gives the due date as 'Continuous' and states the programme accepts applications on a seasonal basis with the intake open date specific to each individual university. For the 2026/27 cycle the University of Alberta set Thursday, July 23, 2026 (applications via the GSMS Awards Portal, referees via the reference Google Form). At the University of Calgary the competition runs through the Graduate Award Competition, which opens November 1 each year, with deadlines that vary by programme and a Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline of February 1.
official.application_cycle: 2026/27 competition (Program Guidelines updated October 2025); recipients may commence the scholarship on September 1, 2026 or January 1, 2027
official.status_note: Alberta Innovates lists Program Status: Active and Intake Status: Open, with due date 'Continuous'; the intake is seasonal and each participating university sets its own open date and deadlines.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 2026/27 Program Guidelines, p.4: 'The scholarship is intended to support the recipient in concentrating their full-time attention to the proposed research. In addition to living expenses, tuition, etc., recipients are encouraged to use a portion of the scholarship for the following...'
benefits: Master's students receive a stipend of $26,000 per year (up to two years); doctoral students receive $31,000 per year (up to four years)
Programme overview publishes funding ranging from $12,000 to $31,000 per year, with terms varying from one to four years depending on the recipient's time in the program

Major (i.e., NSERC) award top-up of $12,000 for students who also hold a major award; at the University of Alberta a major award is valued at $21,000 or higher, at the University of Calgary at $17,500 or higher

AGES top-up for students awarded both an Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship and an AI GSS; published as $18,000 at the University of Calgary, with the amount determined by each university's Faculty of Graduate Studies

Recipients are encouraged to use a portion of the scholarship for conference and relocation travel, scientific materials and books, supplies and expendables, computer hardware and software, facility-use and publication costs
Recipients are invited to Alberta Innovates professional development opportunities (workshops, events) aimed at work readiness, entrepreneurship and employer networking
eligibility: Open to Canadian, permanent resident and international students; there are no citizenship restrictions on this award
Full-time research-based master's or doctoral study at Athabasca University, Concordia University of Edmonton, the University of Alberta, the University of Calgary, or the University of Lethbridge
Proposed research must advance an Applied Digital & Emerging Technology area in natural sciences and engineering (development of the technology itself, not merely using it as a tool)
Each candidate must be sponsored by a faculty supervisor with a record of productive research in one of the eligible areas and sufficient resources for satisfactory conduct of the research

Students cannot simultaneously hold support from more than one Alberta Innovates studentship program, and no more than four years of combined master's/doctoral support from Alberta Innovates across all programs
At the University of Alberta a minimum 3.5 GPA is required, with master's applicants admitted no earlier than Spring 2025 and doctoral applicants no earlier than Spring 2023
requirements: Faculty supervisor sponsorship with adequate research resources

Must clearly articulate how the research aligns with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and how it can produce potential environmental, health, economic, social and other impacts for Alberta

Must articulate in the application how the student will engage with industry during graduate studies and how they will develop professional skills (leadership, communication, collaboration, entrepreneurship)
Apply through the chosen university's own graduate awards competition; applicants do not apply directly to Alberta Innovates
Satisfactory annual progress reporting for renewal, plus a final report to Alberta Innovates after the award term ends
Prior written university approval for significant changes to supervisor, project, department or program of study
documents: University-specific application: the Alberta Innovates GSS Application Form via the GSMS Awards Portal (University of Alberta) or the Graduate Award Competition Application via the Student Centre (University of Calgary)
Up-to-date transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate studies, including transfer credit; official copies required from institutions other than the home university, with grading legend

Two letters of reference (University of Alberta, submitted by referees via the reference Google Form) or reference letters requested and tracked in the Student Awards Application (University of Calgary)
University of Calgary student number (UCID), obtained after submitting the admissions application
Athabasca University applicants only: a cover letter including a program plan/schedule signed by the faculty Dean, project supervisor, Dean of Graduate Studies, or approved designate
selection_criteria: Excellence and strategic alignment in applied digital and emerging technology areas of scientific research important to Alberta
Clear articulation of the potential economic, health, environmental and social impacts of the research for Alberta, including application to Alberta's current or emerging industries and challenges
Evidence of planned industry engagement and professional skills development during the project
University committee review followed by Alberta Innovates staff and external expert reviewer assessment; all investment decisions are at the sole discretion of Alberta Innovates
coverage: Living expenses and tuition, as the stated basis of the stipend ('In addition to living expenses, tuition, etc.')
Travel expenses to attend scientific meetings and conferences
Purchase of scientific materials, books, periodicals and journals; supplies and expendables
Computer hardware and software; costs for the use of libraries, computer and animal facilities
Costs associated with the publication of research results
application_method: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for full descriptions and application details
Submit your application to your institution (University of Alberta: GSMS Awards Portal; University of Calgary: Student Centre, Apply for Graduate Funding, then Graduate Award Competition Application)
Wait for your application to be reviewed and forwarded by the university to Alberta Innovates for alignment assessment
official.application_route: Apply through your chosen Alberta university's graduate awards competition (one application covers all awards at that institution); Alberta Innovates does not accept direct applications.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restrictions - open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and international students; the scholarship is valid only at the five named Alberta universities.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible; the programme is explicitly open to Canadian, permanent resident and international graduate students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research must advance an Applied Digital & Emerging Technology area (information and communications technologies or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies) in natural sciences and engineering, in and of itself or in support of the thematic areas of health/agricultural/life science innovation; advanced materials, defence and aerospace; or natural resource recovery.
official.research_requirement: Full-time thesis-based research developing or advancing the emerging technology itself (projects that merely use ET as a tool are ineligible); faculty supervisor sponsorship required; the application must articulate Alberta impact, industry engagement and professional skills development.
official.duration: Master's: up to two years at $26,000 per year; doctoral: up to four years at $31,000 per year; terms vary from one to four years depending on time already spent in the programme, and recipients may start September 1, 2026 or January 1, 2027.
official.description: Alberta Advanced Education, in partnership with Alberta Innovates, invests in academically superior graduate students undertaking full-time research education at an Alberta university, leading to a research-based master's or doctoral degree. The programme provides funding to enable full-time graduate students to research emerging technologies at participating post-secondary institutions, supporting success in applied digital and emerging technology areas of scientific research that are strategically important to Alberta.
official.program_type: Government (provincial) scholarship - Alberta Innovates program administered by the participating Alberta universities

not_confirmed: deadline_central - Alberta Innovates publishes no single central deadline (due date 'Continuous', seasonal intake, university-specific open dates)
english_requirement - neither Alberta Innovates nor the participating institutions publish an English-language requirement specific to this scholarship
verification.notes: Stipend values ($26,000 master's / $31,000 doctoral), coverage wording, eligibility, term limits and reporting rules were read from Alberta Innovates' 2026/27 GSS Program Guidelines PDF and programme page; institutional deadlines, portals, GPA rule and top-up values were cross-checked on the University of Alberta and University of Calgary official award pages.

applicant_utility.summary: The Alberta Innovates GSS pays $26,000 a year to master's students and $31,000 a year to doctoral students, but you apply through your own university's graduate awards competition - Alberta Innovates never takes applications directly. Because each of the five Alberta institutions runs its own window and portal, pin down your university's dates before drafting: the University of Alberta's 2026/27 competition closed on July 23, 2026, while the University of Calgary's Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 each year with programme-level cut-offs. The deciding factor is not grades alone but whether your project genuinely develops the emerging technology itself rather than merely using it as a tool, and whether you can spell out concrete environmental, health, economic or social impacts for Alberta plus a credible plan to engage industry.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Thesis-based master's or PhD students in natural sciences or engineering at an Alberta university whose work advances AI/ML, quantum technologies, cybersecurity, robotics, additive manufacturing, nanomaterials or related emerging technologies - including international students.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your university's intake window and application portal with its faculty of graduate studies before drafting anything
Secure a faculty supervisor with a productive research record in the eligible technology area
Frame the proposal as technology development with named Alberta impacts (industries, environmental or health challenges)
Order official transcripts from every prior institution early, including transfer credit and grading legends

Brief referees early: University of Alberta referees must submit via a Google Form by the same deadline, and University of Calgary references count only if written within eleven months of the February 1 FGS deadline
At the University of Calgary, apply for admission and obtain your UCID before the scholarship application
common_rejection_risks: Framing the project as using AI or advanced materials as a tool rather than developing the technology itself - explicitly ineligible under the guidelines
Missing the university-level deadline; the University of Alberta states no late applications will be accepted and no exceptions made
Incomplete packages (missing transcripts, signatures, pages or reference letters) which are not reviewed at all

Admitting too early: at the University of Alberta, master's admits before Spring 2025 and doctoral admits before Spring 2023 are ineligible, and the term shrinks one year for each year already spent in the programme
Applying from a course-based or professional programme, which is excluded at the University of Calgary
Holding another Alberta Innovates studentship, which bars concurrent support
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is a fixed annual amount rather than a full-cost award, so international tuition above domestic rates, mandatory ancillary fees, relocation and living costs beyond the stipend, and any research expenses beyond the encouraged uses remain the student's responsibility.
applicant_utility.document_audit: The University of Alberta requires transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate study including transfer credit, official copies from every other institution plus the grading legend, and two referees completing a Google Form; self-printed or self-served transcripts are rejected and the package is judged incomplete if anything is missing. At the University of Calgary the programme uploads transcripts for you, but admission references are only reusable if written within eleven months of the February 1 FGS deadline.
alerts: The 'Continuous' due date on the Alberta Innovates page is not rolling admission - the real deadline is set per university and per programme
Award terms are reduced by one year for each academic year already spent in the programme before the scholarship starts, and master's-to-doctoral transfers inherit the master's start date
Renewal for years two to four depends on satisfactory annual progress reporting, and a final report is required to Alberta Innovates after the award ends
Start dates are fixed at September 1 or January 1, and holding a major external award reduces the stipend to a $12,000 top-up until that external funding ends
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit one application to your university's awards office (University of Alberta GSMS portal or University of Calgary Student Centre), the university reviews and forwards it, and Alberta Innovates then adjudicates strategic alignment - with results announced months later (September to December at the University of Calgary).
